meta.description: Six agent tools — check_config, transcribe, synthesize, generate_image, generate_video, job_status — on a classical ASR-to-agent-to-TTS pipeline instead of a Realtime model. Since v0.5 every capability walks a provider chain: subscription plans first (MiniMax M Plan for speech synthesis and images, Qwen Token Plan for transcription and video), then pay-as-you-go fallbacks in order Xiaomi (free TTS), DeepSeek, MiniMax, Qwen whenever an upstream is rate-limited or out of quota; results name the serving provider and list what was skipped. The six ${credential:...} references (MINIMAX_API_KEY, QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_CN_API_KEY, XIAOMI_API_KEY, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY, QIANWEN_API_KEY) resolve only from %USERPROFILE%\.dsh\.credentials.yaml outside the bundle, and template rows must declare inject: [credentials] or they fail at load. Missing references are skipped in the chain. Generated files are saved locally before paths are returned. Verified live: a MiniMax 2056 cap triggered automatic fallback to Xiaomi audio, a Xiaomi synthesis transcribed back correctly by Qwen, and real image and video output. Not verified: the Qwen pay-as-you-go tail of each chain (account is free-tier-only), reconnect after credential rotation, ffmpeg transcoding (absent on this machine), and rendered plugin details. Limits: whole-file audio, no VAD or barge-in, asynchronous video. Since v0.6 a Voice and media bridge page in Settings edits chain order, model ids, voices, and endpoints with immediate effect; the media_bridge_settings tool reads and writes the same config.
